concepts.displayName: Management of an asymptomatic simple breast cyst
concepts.learningObjective: Select no cyst-directed procedure for an imaging-concordant simple breast cyst that is not painful or bothersome.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Initial treatment of a painful simple breast cyst
concepts.learningObjective: Offer needle aspiration for symptom relief from a persistently painful or bothersome, imaging-concordant simple breast cyst.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Select representative sampling after a discharge workup
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile the imaging target and actual sampled site before choosing a method for the remaining mammographic abnormality.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Recognition of suspicious mammographic calcification patterns
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish suspicious calcification morphology and distribution from typically benign patterns without treating any isolated descriptor as a tissue diagnosis.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Recognition of suspicious mammographic mass morphology
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize mass shape and margin combinations that are concerning on mammography while preserving the boundary that imaging morphology is not a tissue diagnosis.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Initial diagnostic imaging of a palpable breast mass at age 30 to 39
concepts.learningObjective: Select diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis with targeted breast ultrasound for the scoped patient age 30 to 39 with a new palpable breast mass.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Core biopsy of a suspicious solid breast mass
concepts.learningObjective: Select image-guided core biopsy for an accessible solid breast mass categorized as suspicious on diagnostic imaging.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Initial imaging of a palpable breast mass under age 30
concepts.learningObjective: Select targeted breast ultrasound as the initial imaging study for the scoped adult patient younger than 30 with a new palpable breast mass.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Observation of a concordant fibroadenoma
concepts.learningObjective: Avoid routine excision of an asymptomatic concordant core-proven fibroadenoma without atypia or phyllodes concern.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Selected drainage of a lactational breast abscess
concepts.learningObjective: Choose image-guided drainage with culture and individualized antibiotic care for a suitable uncomplicated lactational abscess while preserving feeding when contact precautions are met.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Targeted ultrasound for suspected lactational breast abscess
concepts.learningObjective: Select targeted breast ultrasound for a persistent focal inflammatory breast mass during lactation.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Clinical recognition of Mondor disease
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize the characteristic superficial breast or chest-wall venous cord and its underlying superficial thrombophlebitis.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Selective imaging evaluation of suspected Mondor disease
concepts.learningObjective: Select targeted Doppler ultrasound when the superficial venous diagnosis is uncertain and age-appropriate diagnostic breast imaging when focal symptoms require evaluation for underlying pathology.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Supportive management of uncomplicated Mondor disease
concepts.learningObjective: Use supportive care for concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease while recognizing findings that require renewed evaluation.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Choose local care and an appropriate analgesic in a concurrent ulcer
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret the superficial venous findings and integrate the active NSAID-associated marginal-ulcer history when selecting a treatment regimen.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Calcification morphology and distribution
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile calcification morphology, specimen radiography and clip position before accepting a benign breast biopsy as representation of the intended target.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Phyllodes dissemination pattern
concepts.learningObjective: Use phyllodes spread biology and the actual interval targets to select representative tissue for a new distant-staging question without assuming pulmonary origin from imaging.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Persistent palpable breast finding after negative imaging
concepts.learningObjective: Use examination-imaging discordance to select tissue diagnosis after a correctly targeted negative study.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: New cavity finding after phyllodes surgery
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish an uncertain postoperative fluid cavity from its solid component before choosing representative tissue acquisition.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Grade addendum and phyllodes re-excision extent
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile a specialist grade addendum with the current margin map before choosing the faces requiring further clearance.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Feeding after breast drainage
concepts.learningObjective: Use the infant-contact geometry of a drained breast infection to distinguish a local contact precaution from a blanket instruction to stop lactation.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Distinguish wrong-site acquisition from missing breast images
concepts.learningObjective: Correlate a persistent examination finding with the complete imaging acquisition record, then choose a new targeted study rather than archive retrieval or repetition of an adequate mammographic acquisition.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Persistent clinical breast target after completed imaging
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish the target covered by a concordant benign diagnosis from a separate persistent concerning clinical finding, then choose tissue evaluation despite site-correct imaging without a correlate.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Reconcile the acquired study before reordering
concepts.learningObjective: Read acquisition coverage separately from the attached report and choose review of existing target images when that examination has already been recorded.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Targeted ultrasound after negative mammography
concepts.learningObjective: Order targeted ultrasound for an adult at least 40 with a persistent palpable finding after negative diagnostic mammography.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Select representative tissue after a discordant limited sample
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile the actual sampled site and specimen type with the persistent clinical target before choosing a repeat tissue request.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Verify site concordance before interpreting breast imaging
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret clinical and radiology site labels before deciding whether targeted breast imaging has answered the presenting finding.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Biopsy suspicious palpable mass despite negative imaging
concepts.learningObjective: Obtain tissue diagnosis for a persistently suspicious palpable mass despite negative mammography and targeted ultrasound.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Complete an obscured palpable-target acquisition
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret actual tissue coverage rather than report labels and distinguish reacquisition from retrieval or advanced imaging.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Reconcile a benign biopsy with a different palpable lesion
concepts.learningObjective: Match the sampled lesion to the clinical target before choosing further assessment for a concerning imaging-occult finding.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Select diagnostic imaging for pathologic discharge
concepts.learningObjective: Select age- and context-appropriate diagnostic breast imaging for pathologic nipple discharge.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Classify nipple discharge patterns
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish pathologic spontaneous unilateral single-duct discharge from physiologic bilateral multiduct expressed discharge.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Benign phyllodes complete excision
concepts.learningObjective: Identify complete excision without a prescribed fixed-width margin as the benign phyllodes local-treatment target.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Benign phyllodes positive-margin management
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish observation after an isolated positive benign margin from circumstances suggesting residual or transected tumor.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Borderline phyllodes close-margin management
concepts.learningObjective: Apply the approved borderline close-margin counseling categories.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Borderline phyllodes margin target
concepts.learningObjective: Identify the counseling margin target for borderline phyllodes planning.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Phyllodes hematogenous spread pattern
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize the usual hematogenous rather than nodal spread pattern in phyllodes counseling.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Malignant phyllodes close-margin management
concepts.learningObjective: Apply the approved malignant close-margin counseling categories.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Malignant phyllodes margin target
concepts.learningObjective: Identify the counseling margin target for malignant phyllodes planning.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: No routine axillary staging for phyllodes
concepts.learningObjective: Avoid routine axillary staging when nodes are nonsuspicious.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Suspicious-node biopsy exception in phyllodes follow-up
concepts.learningObjective: Identify image-guided needle biopsy before considering axillary dissection for a suspicious node.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

topic.title: Breast — diagnosis, benign and high-risk lesions
topic.scopeIn: Breast imaging/tissue concordance, palpable masses, discharge, cysts, lactational infection, benign/high-risk lesions, fibroepithelial lesions and the complete phyllodes pathway.
topic.scopeOut: Carcinoma, DCIS and Paget belong to breast-cancer. General hereditary testing principles belong to oncology-genetics-principles.
topic.priorityReason: Frequent workup decisions and extensive existing variants demand concordance and redundancy review.
researchAgenda: Discordant target, sample and imaging evidence
Fibroepithelial grade, margins and nodal exceptions
topic.coverageReason: Live identities cover part of this scope. The research agenda flags breadth to check, and the topic worker must judge redundancy and question quality.
topic.testingWeightBasis: Owner-directed editorial estimate of general-surgery testing relevance. No exam percentages or official blueprint weights are asserted.

recordedHolds.reason: The core-after-FNA atom is neck-specific. Its axillary application and priority over excision require direct verification; the general node-needle exception does not prove every core is adequate.
Grade-addendum scope across the continuous lesion is an explicit extension; verify with the breast pathologist and recorded UK guidance.
The recorded atoms establish margin aims/actions, not the exact fascia-versus-muscle operation. Directly verify both posterior-plane option rankings; no claim of verified fascia/muscle equivalence.

before.Presentation: Jamie Taylor, a 50-year-old woman, returns with the firm irregular 4-o'clock breast finding recorded at the earlier visit. The prior biopsy diagram marks an ultrasound lesion at 2 o'clock in the same breast; that specimen contains fibroadenoma without atypia. At the 4-o'clock marker, diagnostic mammography shows no corresponding density, distortion or calcification, and targeted ultrasound shows no solid or cystic correlate.
before.Task: Which next diagnostic plan should be arranged for Jamie Taylor?
Options: Arrange interval breast examination and imaging

after.Presentation: Jamie Taylor, a 50-year-old woman, returns with a persistent discrete breast lump at the same marked site used for an outside core biopsy. Raising the arm draws the overlying skin inward, as documented before the biopsy. The lump is palpable beneath the superficial biopsy tract. The outside slides contain mature fat and scant normal breast tissue. Archived needle images place the sampling notch and clip in the superficial fat plane, while the examination diagram places the lump beneath that plane. At the clinical marker, current diagnostic mammography shows no corresponding density, distortion or calcification; targeted ultrasound shows the superficial clip but no solid or cystic correlate for the palpable lump.
after.Task: Which next diagnostic plan should be arranged for Jamie Taylor?
Options: **KEY:** Repeat tissue sampling under palpation guidance
Repeat tissue sampling under ultrasound guidance
Obtain breast MRI before repeat tissue sampling

before: The benign sampled target is not the concerning examination finding. Representative tissue assessment is still needed even without an imaging correlate.
Further imaging is tempting when the prior core is benign and no current imaging target is seen, but it does not replace tissue assessment of the separate concerning clinical finding in this profile.
Arrange interval breast examination and imaging
Concordant benign histology supports follow-up of the sampled lesion, not clearance of a separate concerning examination finding.
after: **KEY:** Repeat tissue sampling under palpation guidance

The site label is the same, but the depth and specimen do not establish representative sampling of the persistent clinical target. With no imaging correlate for that lump, palpation-directed sampling addresses it.
Repeat tissue sampling under ultrasound guidance
The visible clip is a tempting reproducible target. Its superficial location and the old needle notch do not establish that it marks the clinical lump.
Obtain breast MRI before repeat tissue sampling
Additional imaging may be useful in selected assessments, but it is not an established prerequisite for representative tissue assessment of the persistent, unsampled clinical target in this record.

record.inference: Reconcile the same skin-site label with needle-notch depth, clip depth and actual specimen. Then: Choose sampling of the clinical lump rather than using a visible clip as a substitute target.
record.focus: The scored objective remains representative assessment after benign/nonrepresentative sampling of a different target. The site discrepancy is now depth at one skin site rather than a trivial different clock position.
record.whatChanged: Removed the different-clock-position and classic firm-irregular shortcuts. The competing ultrasound-guided repeat is now attractive because the clip is visible; the key depends on interpreting specimen depth and current absence of a correlate for the actual lump.

note.why: Against the twice-specified 4-o'clock finding, this makes the benign specimen's irrelevance a direct location mismatch. It is valid evidence, but almost no clinical interpretation is needed to discard the reassuring sample.

cues.response: Removed the 2-versus-4-o-clock mismatch. The site label now agrees; depth, specimen and needle-notch provenance must be reconciled.

note.why: This classic concerning examination wording, followed by two modalities with no correlate, points directly toward tissue sampling. It is legitimate clinical evidence rather than a pure zero-knowledge cue, but it leaves little credible competition in this option set.

cues.response: Removed the classic firm-irregular phrase; the key depends on a persistent clinical target not represented by the specimen/visible clip.

fairness.note: Original flag fully resolved: yes. The report explicitly distinguishes absent imaging correlate at the examined site from a benign biopsy at a different site; ambiguous 'negative' wording is absent.
fairness.response: Kept actual absent density/distortion/calcification and absent sonographic correlate for the clinical lump. The clip visibility is stated separately.

fairness.note: Examination-guided tissue sampling is the defensible best offered plan for the concerning palpable finding. MRI is not established as a necessary prerequisite by this record, and surveillance does not resolve the concern.
fairness.response: The new near miss is repeat ultrasound-guided sampling of the visible clip; the key instead addresses the examination target without requiring MRI first.

fairness.note: Two-step reasoning is present in a basic form: recognize that the benign sample does not address the current site and interpret the clinical/imaging mismatch, then select tissue assessment. Nevertheless this is likely easy for PGY-2/3 residents.

fairness.note: Deleting the entire 2-o'clock biopsy history leaves the same classic examination/imaging discordance and the same answer. The extra record discrepancy does not change the decision or substantially strengthen difficulty.
fairness.response: Removing the prior biopsy record would remove the tempting clip target and the evidence that this apparent same-site benign sample is unrepresentative. The history now affects the guidance choice.

fairness.note: No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. Examination-guided sampling avoids inventing an image-visible target. Exact technique should remain subject to clinical assessment rather than be inferred from this editorial review.
fairness.response: Technique remains specialist-assessed; the question does not assert a universal device or use an image target that does not exist.

suggestions.response: Preserved site-specific raw descriptions, including the separate superficial clip and lack of a correlate for the actual lump.

suggestions.note: Use a verified specimen/localization relationship whose interpretation actually changes the next step; avoid a trivially different clock position added to an otherwise unchanged biopsy indication.
suggestions.response: Replaced the clock-position mismatch with a same-site/depth relationship, needle-notch record and tissue composition.

suggestions.note: Compare clinically credible next diagnostic strategies whose ranking depends on the actual examination, localization or sample adequacy. Do not weaken the concerning findings solely to make surveillance tempting and thereby create multiple best answers.
suggestions.response: Compared palpation-guided core, ultrasound-guided clip core and MRI-before-biopsy strategies. No surveillance foil or weaker concerning finding is used to create ambiguity.

suggestions.response: No foundational label or claim of guaranteed resident struggle. The depth/guidance application is submitted for final independent review.

selfCheck.cueAttack: The clip and lump are distinct targets at one skin site. Ultrasound and core words recur in both competing sampling plans; clinically interpreted depth, not clock-position matching, matters.

selfCheck.oneBestAnswer: Existing ACR biopsy and EUSOBI/ASBrS discordance claims support representative tissue assessment. The new depth inference is a draft application, not a universal claim that all clips locate incorrectly or that every clinically benign lump needs biopsy.

record.title: Mammographic mass morphology
fairness: The resident must integrate interval change, scar location and morphology rather than equating palpability or density with the most concerning target. New spiculation away from the scar makes B a defensible first priority. The growing palpable C may also require sampling; the task correctly asks priority rather than exclusivity.

Importance: high-yield breast imaging/clinical correlation. Realism: three targets in one encounter are somewhat constructed but clinically coherent. No nonmedical wording cue reliably identifies B; interpreting the morphology requires knowledge.
suggestions: Keep subsequent evaluation of C explicit in feedback so prioritization is not taught as dismissal. Do not call this an item that establishes only one lesion merits biopsy.

record.title: Calcification morphology and distribution
fairness: The learner must separate successful retrieval of some calcium from radiology-pathology concordance, then select repeat sampling of the unresolved suspicious group. A is defensible despite its clip and specimen-radiograph confirmation. The B and C matches are meaningful clinical correlations, not merely identical answer-label words.

Importance: high-yield breast biopsy adequacy and avoiding false reassurance. Realism: credible multidisciplinary record review. A repeat representative sampling strategy is plausible, although the exact repeat modality versus excision remains a clinical-team decision not fully tested by identical option modalities.
suggestions: Preserve the distinction between calcium retrieval and representation of the suspicious morphology. Confirm the repeat vacuum approach clinically before release; do not infer that it is universally superior to excision in every discordant biopsy.

record.title: Palpable breast mass in the thirties
fairness: Persistent suspicious palpation at the correctly imaged site requires reconciling examination with negative imaging, then choosing tissue acquisition. The negative studies are essential to the misconception being tested and do not simply name the key. Palpation-guided core biopsy is a defensible best option if the focus can be reliably targeted, as the presentation implies.

Importance: high-yield breast assessment and prevention of false reassurance. Realism: credible clinic case. No major option length, category or convergence cue found; difficulty is likely toward the easier end of moderate.
suggestions: Remove the duplicate marker/probe statement in the exhibit if it contributes no additional acquisition detail. Preserve the correctly targeted imaging premise and clearly suspicious examination.

record.title: Benign phyllodes excision planning

cues.phrase: leaving the visible end of that extension in the cavity
cues.why: Names the retained target, directly selecting 'Focused re-excision of the retained segment'.

cues.phrase: A small solid continuation of the same contour remains at the recorded nipple-side cavity edge
cues.why: Repeats confirmation of the sole limited target; it does not create a competing interpretation.

cues.phrase: for a fixed 10-mm rim
cues.why: The rigid numeric formulation makes this alternative look dogmatic next to an apparently tailored key.

fairness: Removing documented gross residual benign phyllodes is plausible. However, focused segment removal versus a mandated circumferential rim or nipple-areolar sacrifice is an easy proportionality choice. The record does not show actual nipple involvement to make central excision competitive.

Importance: moderate; distinguishing gross residual tumor from a microscopic positive margin is useful, but this sits among many overlapping phyllodes items. Realism: retained visible tumor after an unplanned excision is possible; 'full specimen' should not imply that retained tissue itself was examined.
suggestions: Compare equally plausible completion strategies under a genuine uncertainty about residual extent or grade. Avoid making nipple removal a foil without anatomical justification.
Use one decisive residual-tumor observation rather than repeatedly naming the retained segment. Consider merging with the benign-margin scenario while preserving separate objectives if retained.

record.title: Benign phyllodes margin after excision

cues.phrase: no transection
cues.why: Together with intact excision and no residual mass, explicitly excludes the principal reason for further local removal.

cues.phrase: no residual mass
cues.why: Reinforces the simple surveillance-versus-more-treatment route; the radiation alternative is particularly weak for a benign lesion.

fairness: Surveillance can be defensible after intact benign-phyllodes excision with a microscopic involved margin, but this is a single management-rule item, too easy for routine resident difficulty. The necessary completeness data are appropriate clinically; the problem is the weak alternative set.

Importance: useful practice-changing distinction but narrow and duplicated by adjacent items. Realism: strong postoperative-clinic fit. This independent concern does not authorize changing a frozen passed version; manager adjudication is required before any revision.
suggestions: Preserve the frozen version and record the difficulty concern for the manager. Seek explicit basic-role acceptance or develop a separately versioned question with a genuine competing decision.
Replace radiation with a credible postoperative strategy, and make specimen completeness or discordant residual findings consequential rather than supplying an entirely reassuring summary.

record.title: Borderline phyllodes close-margin action

cues.phrase: a lateral re-excision was booked
cues.why: Supplies one required component before the question, making lateral surveillance look inconsistent with the existing plan.

cues.phrase: subsequently identified a malignant component
cues.why: The narrative upgrade strongly signals adding a face to the already planned lateral excision; the only additive plan is the key. This gives a shortcut around knowing the actual margin policy.

fairness: Updating grade and then applying a margin policy could be a useful two-step task. However, the unique ranking of 4-mm and 2-mm margins depends on the malignant-phyllodes re-excision recommendation being used; no policy is stated, and exact margin practices are not safely assumed universal. I am not asserting that the keyed plan is clinically incorrect.

Importance: moderate specialist breast relevance; exact grade-specific margin thresholds are narrower than the general principle. Realism: specialist pathology addenda are plausible, but the apparently unchanged measurements do not themselves supply a universally agreed surgical rule.
suggestions: Name a verified clinical margin policy or provide its relevant recommendation neutrally, then require application to an oriented specimen with a consequential planning choice.
Remove the already booked plan if it merely supplies a component. Compare credible plans without an option that monitors the closest margin while removing a wider one without another reason.

record.title: Malignant phyllodes close-margin action

cues.phrase: every other face is at least 10 mm clear
cues.why: Directly eliminates whole-cavity surgery.

cues.phrase: an uninterrupted pectoral fascial line
cues.why: Combined with normal muscle findings, explicitly argues against both alternatives, which both remove muscle.

cues.phrase: no focal extension from the cavity
cues.why: Further reiterates the exclusion of the shared muscle-resection component in both distractors.

fairness: The key is the only plan sparing apparently uninvolved muscle, so the option set can be solved by proportionality even without knowing phyllodes margin policy. Whether a 4-mm posterior margin needs re-excision requires an explicit supported policy or clinician adjudication; the task assumes that decision already occurred.

Importance: useful principle of targeted margin clearance, but narrow and overlapping with the other deep-plane items. Realism: anatomy is coherent; routine postoperative MRI for this decision needs a stated clinical reason rather than being added to manufacture complexity.
suggestions: Compare realistic posterior strategies, including an appropriate breast/fascia boundary and a clinically credible observation or re-excision alternative under a stated policy.
Do not make both distractors require muscle removal despite repeated absence of muscle involvement. Keep necessary anatomy and remove redundant exclusion statements.

record.title: Axillary surgery in phyllodes
fairness: Adequate targeting, represented nodal tissue, benign cellular findings and interval improvement require a concordance assessment before applying the phyllodes axillary-surgery principle. This is more than simply announcing a negative node. Surveillance is a defensible choice among the options; routine sentinel-node logic from epithelial breast cancer is a credible error.

Importance: useful breast-surgery distinction, although phyllodes is overrepresented in this batch. Realism: credible preoperative clinic review. No decisive nonmedical overlap or option-format cue identified; exact pathology interpretation still needs clinician sign-off.
suggestions: Preserve targeting adequacy and trajectory. Do not generalize this answer to a persistently enlarging or discordantly sampled node.

record.title: A suspicious node in phyllodes

cues.phrase: insufficient remaining tissue for the requested classification panel
cues.why: Reiterates the earlier exhausted-cell-block finding and advertises a tissue-volume solution; it weakens repeat aspiration before its on-site preparation advantage is considered.

fairness: Obtaining more material and choosing an acquisition route are meaningful decisions, but the supplied reason for FNA failure is exhaustion, not a demonstrated need for tissue architecture. Repeat FNA with on-site preparation may therefore be defensible. Core biopsy may be preferable, yet a node adjacent to the axillary vein also requires an identified safe needle path; its depth does not alone settle core versus excision.

Importance: useful diagnostic sampling principle, but the rare phyllodes-node framing adds specialist detail. Realism: indeterminate spindle-cell cytology is plausible; the exact feasibility and classification requirements are missing.
suggestions: State what the pathologist still needs, distinguishing architecture from more cells for ancillary tests. Provide neutral imaging observations establishing feasible acquisition routes.
Compare plans that each could meet the material requirement; remove the duplicate inadequacy sentence rather than concealing the actual failed study.

record.title: Borderline phyllodes operative margin target

cues.phrase: the wall nodule remains similar in size
cues.why: After successful fluid aspiration, the unchanged solid component directly identifies the only option obtaining tissue from the persisting target.

cues.phrase: Core biopsy of the cavity-wall nodule
cues.why: The key is the only new diagnostic acquisition of solid tissue; one competitor repeats fluid aspiration and the other is surveillance despite the task asking for an acquisition.

fairness: Core sampling of the persistent vascular solid nodule is defensible. Distinguishing an aspirated cavity from an unsampled nodule is important, but this version largely names the missing target and asks for its biopsy. Serial ultrasound also does not match 'diagnostic acquisition' as naturally as a tissue procedure.

Importance: high practical value for postoperative mass evaluation, but not specific to borderline phyllodes or a margin target. Realism: plausible clinic course; reassuring old blood does not establish the nature of the solid component.
suggestions: Ask a neutral next diagnostic plan and compare plausible solid-target acquisition strategies, or introduce an actual sampling-concordance problem rather than an obviously unsampled persistent nodule.
Remove redundant cavity-response detail if it does not change the decision. Consider consolidating with other adequacy/discordance items.

record.title: Malignant phyllodes operative margin target

cues.phrase: the underlying muscle sliding independently of the mass
cues.why: Pre-explains that muscle is separable, strongly eliminating the muscle-resection competitor.

cues.phrase: The mass reaches the fascial surface; no focal signal extension is seen within pectoralis
cues.why: Names fascia while explicitly excluding muscle; selecting the middle anatomical extent becomes a matching exercise.

cues.phrase: the deep component remains to be specified
cues.why: Adds task framing rather than new decision information.

fairness: Including fascia while preserving uninvolved muscle is plausible, but this is essentially one plane-selection rule with a clearly inadequate capsule-following foil and an excessive muscle-removal foil. Imaging contact is not proof of invasion, and the exact required deep margin should be clinically reviewed rather than implied by the wording.

Importance: moderate specialist value; substantial overlap with the posterior re-excision item. Realism: a breast-conserving deep-plane plan is credible, while contraction ultrasound as a routine discriminator needs clinician confirmation.
suggestions: Use a clinically realistic interface uncertainty with credible competing resections, supported by actual margin guidance. Avoid describing each distractor's anatomical disqualification.
Remove the operative-planning filler row. Merge overlapping deep-plane objectives if the manager finds no distinct consequential decision.

record.title: Phyllodes dissemination pattern
fairness: The learner must recognize that the pulmonary lesion could change distant staging and distinguish its origin from two prior cancers before committing to local curative surgery. Lung-target tissue is a defensible priority among the offered acquisitions. Other targets remain clinically important but cannot resolve the same distant-disease question.

Importance: high-value general oncologic staging reasoning despite a rare-tumor wrapper. Realism: multidisciplinary clinic planning is plausible. The item presumes a feasible pulmonary core procedure; technical accessibility and safety should be confirmed clinically, but the presented peripheral target does not create an obvious competing key.
suggestions: Preserve the two-prior-primary ambiguity and curative-intent decision. Do not teach that every peripheral lesion must be biopsied by this route regardless of procedural risk.

record.title: Mammographic mass morphology
fairness: Mass B is the best priority: the learner must interpret suspicious morphology in light of interval change and surgical-bed stability rather than choose high density or palpability alone. Each competing target has a plausible concerning feature, and the same action is offered at each site.

Importance: high-yield breast-workup reasoning. Realism: radiologist correlation and interval comparison are credible in surgical clinic. A table is appropriate for the longitudinal comparison, though it is not a substitute for a validated visual-morphology exercise.

Priority is defensible, but it does not establish that the enlarging palpable mass C needs no sampling. The unspecified magnitude and interval of growth limit any stronger claim about C; no confident key error identified for the narrowly prioritized task.
suggestions: Keep the task limited to priority and have clinical sign-off explicitly retain any separate workup needed for C. Do not convert this into a single-biopsy-only policy.

record.title: Calcification morphology and distribution

cues.phrase: No target calcifications in specimen; clip anterior to the mapped group
cues.why: Only group A is explicitly unsampled; the task asks which group needs renewed targeting. A reader can match missing target to repeat sampling without interpreting calcification morphology.

cues.phrase: Target calcifications present; clip centered on the sampled group
cues.why: Both competing groups are explicitly described as successfully targeted; their pathology also explains the calcifications. This completes option-by-option elimination.

fairness: Repeat targeting of A is appropriate, but morphology and the DCIS diagnosis are largely unnecessary to identify the stated technical miss. The answer follows from specimen coverage alone.

Importance: high-yield radiology-pathology concordance. Realism: specimen radiographs and clip maps are appropriate; clip location by itself can be misleading, but absent target calcifications independently supports inadequacy here. Too easy for PGY-2/3 residents.
suggestions: Test a genuine concordance decision after apparently successful sampling, with plausible competing interpretations of what was represented, rather than making only one row explicitly miss its target.
Keep specimen calcification data and avoid treating clip displacement alone as proof of failed acquisition. Remove redundant reassurance for the other rows unless it changes the decision.

record.title: Palpable breast mass in the thirties

cues.phrase: the 3-o'clock palpable site is not shown
cues.why: Explicitly identifies the missing site. Two options repeat that site and two repeat the known wrong site, so half the choices are eliminated without medical knowledge.

cues.phrase: Diagnostic mammography and ultrasound at 12 o'clock
cues.why: Repeats the prior wrong target as a complete alternative even though the task explicitly asks about the current palpable finding.

cues.phrase: Contrast breast MRI and ultrasound at 12 o'clock
cues.why: A second deliberately wrong-site choice pads the matrix. The remaining decision is a straightforward first-line modality rule.

fairness: Diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound is defensible in this nonpregnant 36-year-old. The study/site discrepancy is important but not difficult when the mismatch is fully announced.

Importance: high-yield breast evaluation. Realism: referral-site errors are possible, but two obvious wrong-site plans are not credible resident decisions. Too easy; no definite clinical error identified.
suggestions: Put the correct current site in every option and compare credible next diagnostic plans based on actual mammographic/sonographic findings or discordance.
If wrong-site recognition is deliberately tested as a safety item, seek explicit acceptance of that easy role instead of presenting a four-choice matrix as resident-level two-step reasoning.

record.title: Benign phyllodes excision planning

cues.phrase: Benign: complete excision without a prescribed fixed-width rim.
cues.why: The stem states the rule needed to answer; no phyllodes knowledge is required.

cues.phrase: cut crosses the capsule where the narrow extension begins
cues.why: Directly declares plan A incomplete under the supplied rule.

cues.phrase: removes the least tissue while meeting the stated policy
cues.why: The task selects the smaller of the two complete maps. Plan C additionally sacrifices the nipple-areolar complex, making B the obvious least-harm option.

fairness: B is uniquely correct under the provided policy and constructed maps. Fairness is achieved by turning the exercise into reading comprehension rather than resident-level clinical reasoning.

Importance: complete benign-phyllodes excision is useful, but this policy/map exercise has lower incremental yield within a batch containing numerous phyllodes margin items. Realism: surgical contour planning is plausible; exact millimeter cut maps imply more certainty than an actual preoperative plan. The task introduces 'left-breast' without earlier laterality, a minor continuity gap.
suggestions: Merge with a postoperative specimen-completeness decision or test a clinically meaningful capsular/extent uncertainty using comparable specific surgical plans.

If a policy excerpt is necessary because recommendations differ, retain it but require interpretation beyond selecting the smallest qualifying number. Remove irrelevant borderline/malignant policy clauses from a purely benign task.

record.title: Benign phyllodes margin after excision
fairness: The learner must distinguish tumor at ink from a transected or visibly residual benign lesion, then avoid automatically applying carcinoma margin or radiation rules. The benign grade and intact-excision observations are necessary, not a paraphrase of the surveillance label.
Importance: useful breast-surgery practice, although less central than common breast malignancy decisions. Realism: postoperative pathology/operative/imaging reconciliation fits the clinic setting.

Surveillance is defensible for the specified intact benign excision. Re-excision can still be discussed in individualized care; the broad wording 'should be discussed' is less exclusive than 'recommended next plan'. Exact management requires Melissa's confirmation; no certain clinical error identified. Preserve this frozen version rather than silently edit it.
suggestions: Retain the exact frozen item. Record the discussion-versus-recommendation wording limitation for manager/clinical review rather than changing the passed version in this batch.

record.title: Borderline phyllodes close-margin action

cues.phrase: Borderline: aim 5 mm; below 3 mm supports re-excision.
cues.why: The pre-answer policy states the exact action rule.

cues.phrase: Final reported margin
cues.why: The final column has already reconciled the main specimen and shaves. Reading its sole value below 3 mm gives the key; interpreting specimen coverage is unnecessary.

cues.phrase: No lateral shave in the specimen log
cues.why: Reinforces the only residual close-margin site and points directly to the lateral re-excision option.

fairness: Lateral re-excision follows the supplied policy and final site-specific report. The superior shave is described as covering the full face, so there is no demonstrated residual ambiguity. However, the item counts an interpretation already performed by the pathologist as learner reasoning.

Importance: useful margin reconciliation, but repetitive within this phyllodes-heavy batch. Realism: an oriented reconciliation is credible; exact combined margin reporting needs pathologist confirmation. Too easy for residents.
suggestions: Test a real specimen-orientation or coverage discrepancy that changes the remaining operation, using clinically validated reporting conventions. Do not simply delete a necessary final margin and ask the learner to invent one.
Alternatively merge the borderline target and close-margin items into one meaningful planning decision. Keep any policy needed for fairness, but avoid a task solvable by reading one final number.

record.title: Malignant phyllodes close-margin action

cues.phrase: Malignant: aim 10 mm; below 5 mm supports re-excision.
cues.why: The stem gives the exact rule selecting surgery for the stated 4-mm margin.

cues.phrase: changes the grade to malignant phyllodes; the measured posterior margin remains 4 mm
cues.why: The current grade and number directly plug into the supplied rule; the old grade is not needed to answer the present task.

cues.phrase: should replace
cues.why: Presupposes that the earlier surveillance plan must change, further weakening the surveillance alternative before clinical reasoning.

fairness: Under the supplied policy, posterior re-excision is the intended best recommendation. But the posterior surface is not anatomically characterized: available breast tissue, fascia or chest-wall boundary can affect the actual re-excision decision. The item should not imply a universal mandate independent of that anatomy.

Importance: clinically relevant response to upgraded pathology, but a rare-tumor rule lookup has limited incremental resident yield alongside the other phyllodes tasks. Realism: specialist grade revision is credible. Too easy despite the chronology.
suggestions: Use a neutral 'current local-control plan' task and give the actual posterior operative boundary relevant to further surgery.

Require reconciliation of a substantive grade/extent or specimen issue before applying a policy; avoid merely stating the new grade and action threshold. Compare plausible local-control plans at the same stage.

record.title: Axillary surgery in phyllodes

cues.phrase: without a separate epithelial carcinoma
cues.why: Explicitly excludes the common competing reason for axillary staging.

cues.phrase: no additional axillary target is described
cues.why: An author-level assurance discourages any further axillary procedure.

cues.phrase: Nodal tissue with preserved architecture and reactive follicles; no malignant cells
cues.why: The already-benign interpretation, combined with repeated matching-target and stability assurances, makes no axillary intervention the conspicuously conservative choice.

cues.phrase: radiology and pathology identify the same target
cues.why: States the concordance conclusion the proposed interpretation task would otherwise require.

fairness: No routine axillary staging is defensible in malignant phyllodes with a satisfactorily evaluated reactive node. Necessary benign sampling findings should not be withheld. The problem is that the item supplies the adequacy/concordance conclusions and then tests a familiar single rule.

Importance: useful distinction from epithelial breast carcinoma; eight related phyllodes items have diminishing practical yield. Realism: the target log is plausible, but repeated exclusions are editorial over-scaffolding. Too easy.
suggestions: Retain enough target and tissue observations to establish adequacy, but remove repeated author assurances and require the learner to resolve a meaningful discordance.
Compare clinically credible axillary next steps rather than using full dissection as an unsupported foil. Consider merging with the suspicious-node item.

record.title: A suspicious node in phyllodes

cues.phrase: the post-biopsy clip lies in fat next to the node; no nodal tissue is reported
cues.why: Directly announces the miss. The key is the only choice that samples the actual node now.

cues.phrase: Excision biopsy centered on the existing axillary clip
cues.why: Deliberately targets the object the stem just placed outside the node; this is an obvious wrong-target choice without needing medical knowledge.

fairness: A properly targeted needle biopsy is defensible. The combination of clip location and no nodal tissue supports a failed sample; the problem is not missing data but a caricatured surgical alternative. True excision of the enlarging node could be a reasonable competing approach, depending on accessibility and diagnostic needs.
Importance: high-value general specimen-target concordance principle, more useful than phyllodes-specific recall. Realism: an off-target needle sample is plausible. Too easy as currently phrased.
suggestions: Offer actual node excision rather than excision of a known misplaced clip, and supply accessibility/architecture needs that allow a defensible comparison with repeat image-guided biopsy.
Keep the inadequate-sample evidence; make the next action a real choice instead of restating the missed target.

record.title: Borderline phyllodes operative margin target

cues.phrase: Borderline: aim 5 mm; below 3 mm supports re-excision.
cues.why: Provides the numerical selection rule before the answer.

cues.phrase: with the least additional breast-tissue sacrifice
cues.why: Once map A's 2-mm surface is rejected, the task tells the reader to choose B over the uniformly wider C without clinical knowledge.

cues.phrase: Removes the lateral extension; retains nipple base
cues.why: Only the key's consequence is framed as resolving the extension while preserving a desirable structure; C is framed as extra central-tissue removal.

fairness: B satisfies the constructed policy/map comparison. There is a continuity issue: the presentation says each map removes the lesion, but only B's consequence says it removes 'the lateral extension', which can imply A leaves tumor. Clarify whether that extension is tumor or a planned margin extension.

Importance: initial phyllodes margin planning is useful but this duplicates other supplied-policy tasks and has low incremental yield. Realism: prescribed surgical aims are not guaranteed final histological margins. Too easy.
suggestions: Clarify what each map actually contains and distinguish planned rim from final pathological clearance.

Merge with a margin-management item unless a different consequential decision can be shown. Retain policy access when needed, but remove the smallest-qualifying-number puzzle and compare realistic operations with supported tradeoffs.

record.title: Malignant phyllodes operative margin target

cues.phrase: Malignant: aim 10 mm; below 5 mm supports re-excision.
cues.why: Gives the initial target directly; reading the minimum rim in each row is sufficient.

cues.phrase: while avoiding the additional chest-wall resection shown
cues.why: The task explicitly rules out map C, the only row naming an additional pectoral-muscle segment.

cues.phrase: Breast tissue plus the planned posterior extension
cues.why: The key is presented as the middle amount of tissue removal, exactly matching the instructed target-without-extra-sacrifice rule.

fairness: B is uniquely selected by the stipulated map and policy, but no medical reasoning is required. The difference between initial counseling aim and postoperative re-excision threshold is useful; here the stem and task do all of that interpretation.

Importance: limited incremental value beside the borderline-target and malignant-close-margin items. Realism: posterior tissue planes are insufficiently defined to generalize whether a specified extra rim is achievable without chest-wall resection. Too easy.
suggestions: Replace the explicit avoidance instruction with a neutral operative-planning task and a clinically grounded posterior-plane problem.

Consider merging the initial-target and postoperative-margin distinction into one clinically realistic case. Do not create difficulty by hiding the applicable policy or pretending an exact planned rim guarantees final clearance.

record.title: Phyllodes dissemination pattern
fairness: The learner must recognize that a distant lesion can change curative-intent breast planning, then prioritize tissue that distinguishes metastasis from a separate lung primary. Prior lung adenocarcinoma makes histology genuinely consequential; the three choices are parallel tissue acquisitions.

Importance: high-yield oncologic staging principle, though the phyllodes-specific setting is uncommon. Realism: clinic staging before proposed local treatment is credible. A peripheral pulmonary target makes image-guided acquisition plausible without an artificial availability assurance.

Pulmonary sampling is the best priority among these options if technically feasible. Actual lesion size, accessibility and biopsy risk would matter in practice, and staging other suspicious sites is not excluded. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline.
suggestions: Retain the competing prior malignancy and curative-intent consequence. At clinical sign-off, confirm that the proposed lung target is safely accessible and that priority does not imply abandoning the node or breast-bed workup.

record.title: Feeding after drainage

cues.phrase: the infant's mouth remains below the dressing; the dressing stays adherent around the opening
cues.why: This explicitly favorable contact description maps directly to continuing direct feeding. A reader can make the clean-versus-dirty distinction without identifying a clinical mechanism.

cues.phrase: Drainage from the opening reaches the flange's inner breast-contact surface and runs toward the milk tunnel.
cues.why: The visibly dirty collection path maps directly to discarding expressed milk. Combined with the favorable latch description, ordinary contamination reasoning selects the complete key without a second resident-level inference.

cues.phrase: The tunnel and bottle remain connected to that flange throughout expression.
cues.why: This additional linkage reinforces the same contamination answer. It clarifies exposure but adds no independent decision or competing interpretation.

fairness: Node node.n3.lactation-drain-contact-boundary.v1: continuing the observed direct feed and discarding milk collected with the described contaminated setup is the single best offered plan. Healthy term infant status, the covered opening, observed latch and pump contact are supplied.

The complete four-option matrix balances each feed/discard component equally. There is no frequency convergence, uniquely comprehensive option, grammar outlier, diagnosis-to-option lexical match or rhetorical absolute. The shortcut arises from the very explicit clean/contaminated route descriptions, not an unbalanced matrix.

Giving the expressed milk disregards the described wound-drainage exposure; pausing the observed direct feed treats the protected latch as though it had the same contact. Neither alternative is equally supported by this record. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified in the assessed fields.

There are two route judgments, but each applies the same immediately visible contact distinction. Counting them as two consequential reasoning steps overstates the cognitive demand. The unusual setting may require knowledge of MRSA feeding precautions, but the options and exhibit make the answer accessible through common-sense contamination avoidance.

The task is appropriately limited to the observed arrangements and next feed. The verdict does not imply that every future expression setup is unsafe or that every infant shares this patient's circumstances.
suggestions: Keep the complete balanced matrix and necessary contact observations; do not obscure whether drainage reaches the collection path to manufacture difficulty.

For a resident-level revision, test a supported concrete next action after a specified change in wound coverage or equipment contact, so reassessment changes the feeding/collection plan rather than asking two restatements of the same contact rule. State the actual arrangement and keep all options at that same decision stage.

If the exact objective is simply recognizing safe versus contaminated routes, seek explicit foundational/safety-item acceptance and label the difficulty easy. Cosmetic removal of the collection-path sentence will not create a second consequential step.

record.title: A sample from the right place on the skin, but what depth?

cues.phrase: The lump is palpable beneath the superficial biopsy tract.
cues.why: Directly states the depth mismatch and repeats 'palpable', making 'palpation guidance' an accessible word-family match. The later archived-image sentence states the same mismatch again, reducing the need to reconcile independent observations.

cues.phrase: Archived needle images place the sampling notch and clip in the superficial fat plane, while the examination diagram places the lump beneath that plane.
cues.why: Explicitly assembles the wrong-depth conclusion for the learner. It is useful provenance evidence, but merely substituting depth for a different clock position does not prevent a basic location-mismatch shortcut.

cues.phrase: targeted ultrasound shows the superficial clip but no solid or cystic correlate for the palpable lump
cues.why: This necessary target-visibility finding directly weakens ultrasound guidance and reinforces palpation guidance. Against an MRI-before-sampling option and an untargetable ultrasound option, the key remains easy to isolate. Do not delete the no-correlate finding to make ultrasound appear falsely feasible.

cues.phrase: Obtain breast MRI before repeat tissue sampling
cues.why: All three options already concede repeat tissue sampling. Only this one inserts an additional preliminary step, so the option set itself gives away the main diagnostic decision and leaves a simple guidance/precondition comparison.

fairness: Original flag fully resolved: yes. Imaging findings are described at the clinical marker; absent density/distortion/calcification and absent sonographic mass correlate are distinguished from the visible clip. The ambiguous bare word 'negative' is gone.

Palpation-guided repeat tissue assessment is the best offered plan for a persistent concerning palpable target not represented by the prior specimen. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified in that broad recommendation.

The ultrasound-guided option does not explicitly say it samples the superficial clip. That target cannot be silently assigned from author rationale; a clinician might use ultrasound assistance during another localization strategy. As written there is no demonstrated sonographic lump target, so it remains weaker, but the proposed near-miss is underspecified.

Two steps are present in a basic form: assess specimen/target concordance, then choose guidance for representative sampling. Explicit repeated depth contrasts and lack of an image target make this likely easy for PGY-2/3.

Skin retraction preceding biopsy is a meaningful concern and avoids attributing it to biopsy scarring. Do not remove this observation merely to make surveillance an attractive but potentially unsafe foil.
suggestions: Remove the redundant sentence that already states the lump lies beneath the biopsy tract; let the archive localization and examination record supply the relationship once.
Make every sampling option explicit about its actual target and guidance. Do not rely on a hidden assumption that ultrasound guidance necessarily means sampling the clip.
Use a verified localization or adequacy distinction that changes the next action and has a credible competing strategy. Preserve the necessary absent-correlate and concerning examination findings.

If the intended lesson remains straightforward representative biopsy despite noncorrelative imaging, request foundational-purpose acceptance rather than claiming that a same-site depth mismatch alone produces resident-level struggle.

record.title: Separate a prior benign breast diagnosis from the current palpable finding

cues.phrase: a discrete hard focus with an irregular edge and little mobility
cues.why: The stacked textbook warning features make tissue sampling the immediate resident response. A testwise reader with ordinary familiarity with cancer warning language can also favor the only tissue option. This is primarily a difficulty shortcut, not a claim that suspicious examination findings should be withheld: these observations are necessary to justify the key despite negative imaging. They currently do almost all the discriminating work.

cues.phrase: The mobile nodule at the earlier biopsy site can be felt separately.
cues.why: The prose performs the lesion-separation inference. Together with 'the earlier biopsied nodule is separately visible and unchanged', it explicitly detaches the reassuring biopsy from the current concern twice. Ordinary reading is enough to discard the old benign result as an explanation of the current focus; the learner need not reconcile a genuine target or sampling discrepancy. This is partial scaffolding, not an independent nonmedical proof that biopsy outranks MRI.

cues.phrase: Images document sweeps through the entire current marked area
cues.why: The emphatic coverage statement weakens a repeat-ultrasound choice through a completed-work heuristic. The interval qualifier means the surveillance option is not literally a duplicate study, so the cue does not eliminate it by logic alone. Site-correct acquisition is legitimate decision-critical information and should remain; the problem is the overall easy comparison, not the presence of an adequate negative study.

cues.phrase: Breast-team tissue sampling
cues.why: The key is a broad specialist-endorsed action beside a named imaging technique and a defined follow-up plan. 'Breast-team' supplies a weak authority cue and 'tissue sampling' allows more latitude than the competitors. It is not a uniquely long key, a grammatical giveaway or a generic shared-decision answer, but naming the sampled target would make the comparison more concrete.

fairness: Scope: independently judged question.palpable-breast.negative-mammogram-targeted-us.v1.r4 using only its after Presentation, Current update, Exhibit, Task and Options. The review marker and option position were ignored. Earlier reviews and local source metadata were consulted for history and holds, not as additional learner-visible facts or proof of quality.

One best answer: tissue assessment of the current clinically concerning palpable focus is the defensible best offered action. The negative mammogram and documented site-correct ultrasound do not account for the suspicious examination, and the prior concordant fibroadenoma is a different lesion. The locally recorded claim.gs028c.palpable.biopsy directly supports this boundary. I found no confident second best answer or clinical inaccuracy in this scoped comparison.

MRI is a credible temptation when conventional imaging has no correlate, but no observation here makes MRI the required intermediate step before tissue diagnosis. Interval examination/ultrasound is a real management strategy in other contexts; the strongly concerning current examination makes it weak here. This is not a claim that MRI or surveillance is universally inappropriate for palpable findings.

The intended sampling target can be inferred from the task, but the answer should explicitly identify the current palpable focus. A missing biopsy-device choice is not itself a fairness defect: the evidence supports tissue diagnosis without establishing one universally best technique when no imaging target exists. Do not invent an ultrasound-guided target, mandate excision, or rank devices from this record.

Difficulty: easy for a typical PGY-2/3 and too easy for the requested routine resident challenge. The dominant operation is applying the familiar suspicious-palpable-mass rule. Recognizing suspicious findings and recalling biopsy is not two consequential steps under this standard. Deleting the earlier fibroadenoma history leaves essentially the same question and answer. The negative imaging supplies a useful clinical discordance, but the emphatic examination and explicit separation largely settle it.

Importance and realism: high-yield, practically important breast-surgery reasoning and broadly suitable for ABSITE preparation; no current exam blueprint was checked. Persistent clinical concern despite negative imaging is a useful outpatient breast-clinic scenario. Coexisting fibroadenoma is plausible, but this particular unrelated stable lesion mostly adds reading rather than difficulty. The exhibit is a report table, not an image-interpretation task.

Owner flag: FULLY RESOLVED for the original complaint that an explicitly unassessed ultrasound site gives away a keyed ultrasound request. Current imaging actually covers the current site and ultrasound is no longer the key. This is a changed decision, not validation of the old ultrasound item. The separate resident-difficulty concern remains, so original-flag resolution does not justify PASS.

Source hold touches key: NO declared active key hold in the round-three packet or sources-question-flags2-round3-20261105.json, and the recorded biopsy claim supports the key at its stated scope. The tissue-diagnosis decision has one recorded ACR guideline; ASBrS/SBI guidance supports the separate fibroadenoma's management, not independent corroboration of that biopsy rule. No source was re-accessed. New wording and claims remain needs_clinician_review.

No unique task-to-key lexical match, majority-component convergence, rhetorical absolute, patient-preference giveaway or overt teaching sentence was found. Runtime ordering, wait previews, preceding feedback, complaint fields and actual rendering are outside the supplied after fields and were not audited.
suggestions: Replace the keyed label with 'Biopsy the current palpable left-breast focus'. This specifies an action and target without inventing a device or a nonexistent imaging correlate. Keep the alternatives concrete and at the same next-assessment stage.

Retain the concerning examination and site-correct negative imaging. Remove the redundant second statement that the earlier lesion is separate, and do not count the stable fibroadenoma as an additional inference when its irrelevance is already announced. Wording cleanup alone will not make the item sufficiently challenging.

For a substantive resident-level revision, build a supported clinical-pathology concordance decision in which a prior benign sample plausibly pertains to the current concern, but actual acquisition and specimen observations determine whether it is representative. Compare concrete next plans such as sampling the current concern, additional imaging, and surveillance only when each has a credible role. Require the learner to establish what the prior evidence covers before choosing the next action; do not simply state that the biopsy missed the target. Verify the necessary facts and exact ranking before authoring that replacement.

If retaining this exact clinical decision as foundational breast safety teaching is preferable, request explicit manager acceptance of that educational role. Do not call it hard, invent contraindications to MRI, or remove essential examination findings to manufacture difficulty. Any materially changed scored construct needs the repository's concept-version treatment.

question.stem: Which next diagnostic plan should be arranged for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Repeat tissue sampling under palpation guidance
answerChoices.rationale: The site label is the same, but the depth and specimen do not establish representative sampling of the persistent clinical target. With no imaging correlate for that lump, palpation-directed sampling addresses it.

answerChoices.label: Repeat tissue sampling under ultrasound guidance
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The visible clip is a tempting reproducible target. Its superficial location and the old needle notch do not establish that it marks the clinical lump.

answerChoices.label: Obtain breast MRI before repeat tissue sampling
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Additional imaging may be useful in selected assessments, but it is not an established prerequisite for representative tissue assessment of the persistent, unsampled clinical target in this record.

question.explanation: A matching skin-site label does not establish representative sampling at the correct depth. The specimen, notch and clip relate to superficial fat, while the persistent clinical lump lies beneath that plane. Current imaging identifies the clip but no target corresponding to the lump. Arrange representative tissue assessment directed by examination; repeating the visible clip target would not resolve that localization problem. Technique remains subject to specialist assessment.

question.stem: Which next step is best for the assessment of {patientName}'s current breast finding?

answerChoices.label: Breast-team tissue sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The persistent hard, irregular, poorly mobile clinical focus remains concerning despite completed site-correct imaging. The earlier concordant fibroadenoma is a separate finding, so its benign diagnosis does not settle this target. Tissue assessment is indicated; the breast team selects the sampling method when no imaging target exists.

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced breast MRI
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Additional imaging is a plausible response to discordance between examination and conventional studies. answerChoices.label: Breast examination with interval ultrasonography
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Surveillance is credible for the unchanged, concordant, core-proven fibroadenoma in the record. It does not account for the separate hard, irregular clinical focus. Negative site-correct imaging does not make that examination finding concordantly benign.

question.stem: Which initial care plan best fits {patientName}'s confirmed uncomplicated Mondor disease after appropriate evaluation, without infection, suspicious findings or a separate indication for anticoagulation?

answerChoices.label: Warm compresses, appropriate NSAID, and follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Supportive measures and follow-up fit the confirmed uncomplicated superficial thrombophlebitis after appropriate evaluation.

answerChoices.label: Incision and drainage with empiric antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: The evaluated finding is uncomplicated Mondor disease, without an abscess or infection requiring drainage and antibiotics.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The evaluated finding is uncomplicated Mondor disease, without an abscess or infection requiring drainage and antibiotics.

answerChoices.label: Surgical excision of the involved superficial vein
answerChoices.rationale: Excision of the superficial vein is not routine initial treatment for concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Excision of the superficial vein is not routine initial treatment for concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease.

answerChoices.label: Routine therapeutic anticoagulation
answerChoices.rationale: Routine therapeutic anticoagulation is not standard for uncomplicated Mondor disease without a separate indication.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Routine therapeutic anticoagulation is not standard for uncomplicated Mondor disease without a separate indication.

question.explanation: Offer supportive care for concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease, including warm compresses, an NSAID when appropriate and follow-up. Other treatments require a separate indication.
question.teachingPoint: Concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease is generally self-limited. Initial care is supportive with warm compresses, an NSAID when appropriate, avoidance of irritating activity or clothing, and follow-up. Antibiotics, venous excision, and therapeutic anticoagulation are not routine without a separate indication.

decisionNodes.stem: How should the clinic handle the treating specialist's relevant information request after {patientName} authorizes Mondor-disease care coordination?

answerChoices.label: Share relevant information for authorized care
answerChoices.rationale: The patient has authorized coordination, and the specialist requests relevant information. Share for that purpose while avoiding unnecessary disclosure.

answerChoices.label: Send the complete chart for the specialist to filter
answerChoices.rationale: The whole chart may include information beyond the consultation's purpose. Authorization to coordinate does not justify unnecessary disclosure for the specialist to filter later.

answerChoices.label: Request a new authorization for each relevant chart item
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied authorization already supports relevant coordination. Treating every relevant item as newly prohibited obstructs that authorized care purpose.

answerChoices.label: Send a de-identified summary for the treating consultation
answerChoices.rationale: The specialist needs relevant patient-specific consultation information. A de-identified substitute does not provide the authorized coordination requested in this scenario.

decisionNodes.explanation: Share relevant patient-specific information for the authorized consultation, avoiding unnecessary disclosure. The stated authorization supports that coordination; confidentiality does not require blocking every exchange or sending the entire chart.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Confidentiality permits appropriate exchange for authorized care; it does not prohibit all coordination. Share information relevant to the consultation while avoiding unnecessary disclosure. Remember to match the information to its purpose. Sending the whole chart for someone else to filter, or treating every relevant item as newly forbidden, misses that balance in this supplied setting.
sourceLabels: Confidentiality
Mondor Disease
Mondor's Disease: A Review of the Literature

question.stem: Which initial source-control plan is appropriate for {patientName}'s confirmed uncomplicated drainable collection?

answerChoices.label: Continue antibiotic treatment without drainage
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Antibiotics alone do not provide source control for this confirmed drainable abscess.

answerChoices.label: Stop breastfeeding from the affected breast
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Feeding or expressed milk can generally continue when the infant and pump avoid purulent drainage, open infected tissue, and the drain site.

caseNodeContexts.task: Which imaging plan best addresses this patient's focal symptoms and concern for underlying pathology?
caseNodeContexts.presentation: {patientName}, a 44-year-old woman, presents with new focal, noncyclic burning pain and a palpable superficial breast cord. There was no clear procedure or trauma.
caseNodeContexts.caseName: Clinic Patient: Focal Breast Cord Evaluation

node.stem: Which imaging plan best addresses this patient's focal symptoms and concern for underlying pathology?

answerChoices.label: Diagnostic mammography and targeted Doppler ultrasound
Contrast-enhanced breast MRI as the sole initial study
Immediate excisional biopsy without diagnostic imaging

node.explanation: Targeted high-frequency ultrasound with color Doppler can demonstrate the thrombosed superficial vein when the diagnosis is uncertain. For this patient with clinically significant focal breast symptoms and concern for underlying pathology, diagnostic mammography or tomosynthesis plus targeted ultrasound is appropriate; routine screening, MRI alone, or biopsy before diagnostic imaging does not answer the initial question.
sourceLabels: Rountree, Barazi, and Aulick, Mondor Disease, StatPearls, updated 2023
Amano and Shimizu, Mondor's Disease: A Review of the Literature, 2018
ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Breast Pain, 2018
Clinically approved by Melissa Rowland, MD on 2026-08-06

resultGateAfter.resultNarrative: Diagnostic mammography shows no suspicious breast lesion. Targeted ultrasound with color Doppler demonstrates a noncompressible superficial tubular structure without internal flow, concordant with superficial thrombophlebitis, and no abscess. There is no known hypercoagulable condition.

decisionNodes.stem: What initial management should you recommend for this patient now?

answerChoices.label: Warm compresses, appropriate NSAID, and follow-up
Incision and drainage with empiric antibiotics
Surgical excision of the involved superficial vein

decisionNodes.explanation: Concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease is generally self-limited. Initial care is supportive with warm compresses, an NSAID when appropriate, avoidance of irritating activity or clothing, and follow-up. Antibiotics, venous excision, and therapeutic anticoagulation are not routine without a separate indication.
sourceLabels: Rountree, Barazi, and Aulick, Mondor Disease, StatPearls, updated 2023

ACR Appropriateness Criteria: Breast Pain, 2018
Clinically approved by Melissa Rowland, MD on 2026-08-06

Fever with a fluctuant breast collection
A suspicious breast mass with axillary adenopathy

node.explanation: Concordant uncomplicated Mondor disease is generally self-limited. Initial care is supportive with warm compresses, an NSAID when appropriate, avoidance of irritating activity or clothing, and follow-up. Antibiotics, venous excision, and therapeutic anticoagulation are not routine without a separate indication.
